decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom is only scheduled for release in Q1/2019, so with no market evidence to compare against aspirations, management will carry this strategic product using its slack.
Small volume chambers are core consumables in the firm's established dosimetry portfolio with steady clinical demand, so no shortfall triggers problemistic search.
This second small volume chamber fills a niche in the line at low carrying cost, though its overlap with B gives a slightly higher risk of consolidation.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is a staple product that likely meets aspiration levels drawn from the firm's past performance.
Relative dosimetry chambers complement water phantom systems and support system sales, so dropping it would not free meaningful resources.
Thimble chambers are a long-established product category with predictable demand, so management has no reason to withdraw it in its first year.
